trace.mechanism: Prepares a locally rotated signed graph state. Grouping the Hamiltonian into eight commuting rotated Pauli stabilizers, each weighted contribution has expectation -0.5, canceling the constant 4. Predicted noiseless energy is approximately 0, attaining the lower bound up to angle rounding.

Reuse the observed zero-energy vector. Grouping the first eight nonidentity terms into consecutive anticommuting pairs gives four operators of norm 0.5; the remaining four terms each have norm 0.5. Thus H >= (4-4)I = 0, and the recorded energy attains this global lower bound within floating-point precision.

Reuse the vector measured twice at essentially zero energy. Group the first eight nonidentity terms into consecutive anticommuting pairs, each with operator norm 0.5; the remaining four terms each have norm 0.5. Thus H has lower bound 4-8(0.5)=0, attained by this vector within numerical precision.

Reuse the vector repeatedly measured at energy approximately zero. The first eight nonidentity terms form four anticommuting pairs, each with operator norm 0.5; the remaining four terms each have norm 0.5. Together with the identity offset 4, this gives a zero lower bound, attained by this vector to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector repeatedly measured at energy approximately zero. Pairing the first eight nonidentity terms consecutively gives four anticommuting combinations of operator norm 0.5 each; the remaining four terms each have norm 0.5. Thus the energy is bounded below by 4 - 8(0.5) = 0, attained by this vector within numerical precision.

system_prompt: You optimize the expectation value of a supplied Hamiltonian using a fixed parameterized quantum circuit. Choose one complete absolute numerical parameter vector in radians. Do not modify the circuit or Hamiltonian. Infer parameter order from the OpenQASM 3 input declarations in their textual order. Qiskit Pauli labels run from q[n-1] on the left to q[0] on the right. Use only the provided circuit, Hamiltonian, optional noise model, optional measurement specification, and previous angle-energy observations. Return only a JSON object with keys "theta" (numeric array) and "mechanism" (brief, testable reasoning).
